correctness.rationale: The covariance of uniform area on an n-gon follows from explicit equal-area triangular moments and dihedral symmetry. Its inverse gives K(x,y)=1+c x·y. Convexity bounds the L-infinity norm by any vertex row; a vertex sign input gives equality, and kernel symmetry yields L1 dual equality. The negative cap is reconstructed by two edge intersections; shoelace area and x-first-moment identities give the exact norm. For the limit, uniform radial expansion r_n=1+(s²-δ²)/2+O(δ⁴), angular averaging against a Lipschitz integrand, differentiability in c, and exact disk-cap integrals produce the coefficient 5π√15/12. There is no leap from samples to infinite claims. The packaged checker separately passed 15 groups: three exact rational identities, four independent triangle-quadrature comparisons, five coefficient-scaling comparisons, and three floating reproductions of the rational benchmarks.

value.rationale: Affine least-squares projection on a simple polygon is a canonical local approximation operator, and regular n-gons converge to the disk in a controlled geometric way. Exact norms across the entire discrete family and the evaluated nonzero n^-2 discrepancy offer a motivated, interpretable benchmark for worst-case pointwise stability and shape approximation. The calculation extends beyond the already-known triangle, parallelogram and disk cases; it is not simply another rational numerical instance.
